correctness.rationale: The identity block makes the message-to-codeword map injective. For sum zero the nonzero r-tuples summing to zero have count M_r=(q−1)^(r−1)−M_(r−1) for r≥1, with M_0=1, giving the stated B. To check H independently, for sum s≠0 expand the product of the per-pair factor z²+(z−z²)1_{u_i∈{0,s}}. For a specified r<k marked positions there are 2^r q^(k−r−1) messages of each fixed sum s, because an unmarked coordinate can enforce that sum. For r=k, if j positions equal s the constraint is (j−1)s=0; summing over nonzero s gives S_(k,q)−2^k. Completing the binomial expansion for r<k and adjusting its r=k term gives H as printed. The last coordinate is nonzero exactly on the second class, giving zH. Counting solutions of the cyclic congruence uses gcd, not a field property. For k≥5 the nonzero-sum part cannot contribute to weight four or below; the zero-sum part has no weight two and exactly binom(k,2)(q−1) words of weight four. These arguments cover q=2 and composite q as well.
